verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "A checkpoint operation takes content from the WAL file and transfers it back into the original database file."

verdicts.claim: Automatic checkpoints are PASSIVE and run after commits once the per-connection WAL threshold is reached; the default is 1000 f
verdicts.evidence: wal_autocheckpoint: "defaults to having the auto-checkpoint enabled with a threshold of 1000 ... pages"; "Checkpoints initiated by this mechanism are PASSIVE"; "zero or a negative value ... disables automatic checkpoints entirely"

verdicts.evidence: wal_checkpoint_v2: "The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode ... passive mode might leave the checkpoint unfinished"

verdicts.claim: FULL waits for the writer to finish and readers to use the newest snapshot, then copies all frames and syncs the database; i
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: FULL "blocks ... until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot ... FULL blocks concurrent writers while it is running"

verdicts.claim: RESTART adds waiting for readers to stop using the WAL, ensuring the next writer can reuse it; TRUNCATE additionally reduces
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: RESTART "blocks ... until all readers are finished with the log file"; TRUNCATE "the WAL file is truncated to zero bytes upon successful completion"

verdicts.claim: A reader's snapshot limits checkpoint progress. Long-running or continuously overlapping readers can prevent WAL recycling
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "if ... there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound"

verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "It is fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) and later. Backports of the fix are available for some earlier releases: 3.44.6 and 3.50.7"; "the database file goes corrupt"
